subject.title: Cron session accumulation can silently exhaust agent context window — no guardrails or warnings

question: Should #38730 stay as the umbrella for both isolated cron base-session retention and recurring-job cadence/context guardrails, or should maintainers close it in favor of narrower canonical issues after selecting PR #90194 and PR #89739 outcomes?
rationale: Current source proves the retention gap, but active related PRs intentionally disagree about base-row preservation and add a new cadence config surface, so automation cannot safely choose the product contract.

options.title: Keep umbrella until slices land
options.body: Keep #38730 open while reviewing #90194 for orphan/base retention and #89739 for cadence limits, then close it only when the combined guardrail story is explicit.

options.title: Narrow to retention only
options.body: Declare #89666/#90194 the canonical retention path and move cadence/context warnings to a separate follow-up before closing this umbrella.

options.title: Preserve current base rows
options.body: Reject base-row pruning as too risky and keep only warning/min-interval guardrails, accepting that orphan cleanup needs a different owner or migration design.

recommendation.title: Keep umbrella until slices land
recommendation.body: Keep #38730 open while reviewing #90194 for orphan/base retention and #89739 for cadence limits, then close it only when the combined guardrail story is explicit.

likelyOwner.reason: This person is the most recent visible owner in current blame for the localized cron/session code and is well placed to route the maintainer decision across the active PRs.
